campaign.name: And Then the Dragons Came: Purewater
campaign.description: A Classic Fantasy Imperative port of 'And then the Dragons Came', relocated to Purewater -- a Venice-like canal city where the sacred waters of the Lake Lady meet the sea. Baron Hanzo di Teufel arrives with his Dragon Knights for the Lake Lady's Tourney, his possessed champion concealed among them. Four strangers arrive the same week. Built as a living world: every NPC and faction runs its own agenda on a clock, and what the party does not witness happens anyway.

acts.title: FIRST CUSTOMERS AND THE MIDNIGHT EXCHANGE / A ROAD PEOPLE CAN USE
acts.for: Hrill: Give Hrill a practical accomplishment at a broken crossing, then a journey through isolated communities. His calm, persuasion and judgement can get people working together; his physical skills matter. Discover why Vaust's offer of protection attracts support. Reach the hospice, learn the two possible routes, and decide whether to take any continuing role. No job is accepted for him.
acts.takes: Hrill: At risk are a stranded traveller, medicine and a usable crossing; subsequently access and local trust. Losses require actual choices and resolution. No compulsory rescue failure, guilt, recruitment or combat.

acts.title: THE ASHWICK PAPERS / THE PRICE OF ORDER
acts.for: Hrill: Explore Wind Stair and Alder Hame, discover the difference between Vaust's public road scheme and his coercive programme, and contest its actual dependencies. Military knowledge can identify what the camp is preparing. Hrill can negotiate, organise, investigate, bypass the camp or seek genuine Crown assistance. He decides what loyalty and ending the killing require. Shared global context: imperial restorationists need willing communities, routes and stolen spiritual heritage; Nimras's separate venture is not a prerequisite and nobody knows his discoveries.
acts.takes: Hrill: At risk are freedom of movement, homes, local consent and specific people during a possible armed eviction. Threats need warnings, means and earned information. Peaceful settlements and early antagonist defeat can end this act.

acts.title: THE UNBOUND DEAD / WHAT THE ROAD IS FOR
acts.for: Hrill: Turn surviving discoveries and alliances into a decisive opportunity: establish a community-controlled route, prevent a surviving eviction or intercept the actual relic wagon. The restored route and independent communities are lasting gains. Relic restitution is possible without undertaking a global war. A defeated Vaust stays defeated; no mandatory working, monster, replacement boss or last fight.
acts.takes: Hrill: At risk are the particular route, people and assets still contested. Clear victory, negotiated protection, partial recovery and withdrawal stand. The Dragon Kings' return is an opposed project, never an inevitable consequence.

acts.title: THE LONG SHORE / PARALLEL NIMRAS
acts.for: Hrill: Meet Edda through Maelin at Three Hearths, negotiate actual work, travel to Hythe and join a supply boat. Explore unfamiliar shores before discovering the great animal. Secure Bell Reed landing and deliver real supplies. Physical clues, local accounts and a hunter's preparations reveal overlapping dangers.
acts.takes: Hrill: Lives, cargo, equipment, wages and the boat can be lost through actual hazards or enemy action. Warnings, shelter, rope, competent crew and retreat work. No compulsory wreck, fight, accepted employment or first sight of the animal.

acts.title: THE LONG SHORE / PARALLEL NIMRAS
acts.for: Hrill: Explore White Shingle and Narrow Water, observe the reedback, learn the seasonal channel and make contact with Ilyen's independent shore community. Garr's finite hunting expedition competes for these waters. Hrill can protect a crew, investigate, negotiate, expose or disable actual hunting capacity, and earn access to older resistance history and routes.
acts.takes: Hrill: The animal, fishers' livelihood, shore access and people aboard boats face cold water, entanglement, armed interference and a possible harpoon attempt. No secret universal ritual, automatic hostile elves, prescribed betrayal or claim that all earlier military service was wrong.

acts.title: THE LONG SHORE / PARALLEL NIMRAS
acts.for: Hrill: Use earned knowledge and alliances to establish a safe northern supply route and settle surviving conflict. Options include preventing a hunt, freeing an actually entangled animal, protecting a consenting community's access or arranging an enforceable practical agreement. Early solutions can end the story.
acts.takes: Hrill: Confront only surviving operations with real means and intelligence. Loss, withdrawal, partial success and lasting peaceful victory all stand. Nobody must fight the animal or undertake a larger imperial war. No replacement villain appears because Hrill successfully settled the conflict.

due_beats.title: Maro Quist reads it to the end
due_beats.summary: The magistrate reads everything put in front of him, at his own pace, while you wait -- and then explains accurately why it is not his to act on
due_beats.onscreen_if: On an actual petition presented to Maro Quist; date is opportunity backstop, not an invented offscreen petitioner.
due_beats.narrative:
**The wall, in the person of a decent man.**

Seventy-one, upright, chain always worn. He does not interrupt and cannot be
interrupted. He reads the whole thing -- actually reads it, in front of you, at
his own pace, while you stand there -- and then repeats your position back to
you more accurately than you put it.

And then tells you exactly why it is not his.

The watch is under a written standing order. He is not corrupt, he is not
frightened, and he is not persuadable, because he is **right**. A baron's son
with a knife is weather, and you do not sue the weather.

If he reads it twice, he has changed his mind, and the room should know it.

due_beats.title: Ivo Calder folds
due_beats.summary: The assayer who signed what he should not have has kept his original notes, moved them twice, and collapses completely the moment an independent reading appears
due_beats.narrative:
Fifty, distinguished, guild indigo, instruments kept beautifully, and he has
not slept properly in six weeks.

He has the whole defence prepared and wants to deliver it; a question he has not
anticipated stops him dead. What he wants is to be told that what he signed was
reasonable.

**There is no middle with him.** Vigorous defence, and then everything, in one
breath, the moment an independent reading appears. He has not destroyed the
original notes and has moved them twice.

What this buys is **a name** -- who is actually paying the Baron -- not a
conviction. The man who is paying is not in this city and does not die on the
sand.

actual introduction by Maelin at ThreeHearths. Place: established hospice courtyard,
two gates, hearth/kitchen, practical rough shore sketch and ordinary supply bales.
